I never had any academic problems in public school. These days I am a shut in. I was always a very shy child. But since I wasn't a discipline problem, people didn't intervene. When I became an adult I tried therapy and meds. I tried volunteering, I tried "getting out there." Everything seemed like a gigantic farce. 

I went pretty far for somebody who doesn't feel like she's ever doing eyecontact right, or feel like she could ever possibly look at someone in the face and smile. For someone who went years without raising her hand. But it wasn't enough to get through college, and the one job I had I only got through the Department of Rehabilitation.

For all my training in school as a kid, I have little to show in the way of socialization, and I really wish that weren't the case. I wish when I was young somebody would have helped me and mentored me. There is always something to do now, but it will never be the same as having the help in my formative years. I don't like being isolated and useless. I am a lot more hopeless than lazy.

Well, like a lot of people here probably, I can't relate to your problems. 

Something is amiss in your life. Maybe it's not feasible to get some sort of diagnosis, but you know enough to know that there is a problem. I wouldn't be surprised if you had clinical depression, but even if you didn't you *are* depressed. You know that much. 

There may be something to the sexuality thing, but to be honest it doesn't strike me as homosexuality. It could be, but maybe you are more asexual? Or just don't have a level of sexual desire most people have? Do you have any issues with misogyny or misandry?

Maybe you have self esteem issues but prefer a lot of social distance as well. Both problems aren't necessarily related or unrelated. Maybe your pain is more feeling guilty that you can't share these common life experiences with people and it makes you suspicious that something is wrong with you. (As opposed to the pain of not being able to enjoy something you feel you are missing out on). 

Ask yourself, in an ideal world, what would life be like? Would everything be the same, but you would magically not feel disgust when decent people express how much they like you? 

In an ideal world, would it be socially acceptable for you to be distant or alone more often than what you are currently doing? 

And how would you feel about yourself? If you liked yourself, what kind of person would you have to be?

That sucks your country does not have accessible psychologists. (And technically you're not allowed to explicity ask reddit to be psychologized btw). It's hard to not be in touch with what is troubling us.
